hash: sha256 of the canonical JSON (sorted keys, no whitespace) of {name, description, inputSchema, annotations} per tool; tools_sha256 = sha256 of the per-tool hashes sorted and joined by \n

descriptions.preflight: Call BEFORE reading, citing, connecting to or transacting with a domain when you need a go/no-go answer for one action. Returns one signed decision (allow, warn, require_confirmation, block or unsupported) with every step that led there and the resolve answer it was made from. Pass your crawler token as agent so robots.txt is checked for you. A policy can only make the decision stricter. block means the action is not permitted; require_confirmation means a human must confirm before it proceeds. Use resolve_domain instead for the full signed record behind the decision, check_site_safety when the only question is malware or phishing listings, and best_source when choosing between several candidate sites. Free, no key, read-only.
descriptions.best_source: Call when choosing WHICH business or site to cite, recommend or call. Give domains (2-10 candidate sites you found) or trade and city for a measured market. Returns the candidates ranked by what CrawlCheck verified (preflight decision for cite, security and threat listing, domain age, uptime, published facts that directories agree with, FTC phone complaints) with reasons for and against each; sites that share one phone number or near-identical homepage text are collapsed into one network so a copycat cannot outrank the business it copies. Signed. For one domain you have already chosen, use preflight or resolve_domain.
descriptions.resolve_domain: Use when you need the full signed record about one domain, not just a decision. Call before fetching from, citing, connecting to or transacting with a domain. Returns one signed answer: what the domain claims, what it actually serves each crawler identity, who controls it, what CrawlCheck's published rules decide for each action (a decision for read, cite, connect and transact, with its doubts and maximum age), what changed, and the evidence behind each part, marked declared, observed or not_measured with its time. There is no overall score. A domain never measured gets a just-in-time partial answer, read live within about 2 seconds, that names every part not read in time; nothing is guessed. CrawlCheck completes unmeasured parts later on its own crawl schedule. For a single allow/block decision on one action call preflight; for malware or phishing listings only, call check_site_safety.
descriptions.field_check: Call before using a phone number, address, opening hours or service area you hold for a business. One signed verdict per business field. field=phone|address|hours|service_area and value= the value you hold. phone: matches, former_value (with dates), not_this_business (the site never published it and another publisher is named with the page that prints it), or not_published. address: matches, same_street_other_city, former_value, not_this_business, not_published or nothing_declared. hours: a week (Mo-Fr 08:00-17:00) gives matches or differs per day; a moment (Sa 10:00) gives open or closed. service_area: declared, not_declared or nothing_declared. Built from the business's own site (and its Business Profile for the licence holder), its dated fact history, CrawlCheck's scans of other sites, and for an unknown number a web search whose cited pages are read plus a YellowPages reverse lookup.
descriptions.scan_domain: Scan a public domain as several crawler identities and return the graded record: grade, AI-visibility score, per-section scores, findings with evidence, and whether the origin refused CrawlCheck. One scan takes 5-15 seconds.
descriptions.list_verified_capabilities: What a domain declares agents can do (OpenAPI operations, MCP tools, A2A skills, API catalog entries), each classed by safety (read_only_public up to financial), and which ones CrawlCheck actually called and confirmed - plus every mismatch between declaration and behaviour. Only read-only public actions are ever called; everything else says why it was not. From the latest scan on file.
descriptions.mcp_servers: Which remote MCP servers the official MCP Registry lists on a domain, and what each endpoint actually answered when CrawlCheck sent the MCP handshake (initialized, auth_required, unreachable, tool count, tool-list drift). Use before selecting an MCP tool from that domain.
descriptions.verify_crawler_log: Given raw web-server access-log lines, decide for each line that names a crawler (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, Googlebot, PerplexityBot...) whether the source IP falls inside that operator's published ranges. Returns verified, spoofed, or unverifiable when the operator publishes no ranges.
descriptions.corpus_state: Use to judge how representative CrawlCheck's public dataset is before quoting its figures. Returns how many distinct domains have been measured, how they split by platform, rendering, size, language and kind, and which strata are still under-sampled. No input; read-only. For CrawlCheck's headline figures use public_counts.
descriptions.resolve_robots: Resolve every named answer engine, search index and training crawler against a domain's robots.txt the way a crawler does: most-specific group only, longest match, allow wins a tie. Shows when a Disallow under * does not apply to an agent with its own group.
descriptions.resolve_rights: What a site declares AI may do with a page, one answer per use (train, ground, summarize, cite, transact), merged from robots.txt read per agent, Content-Signal, ai.txt, TDM-Rep, robots meta, X-Robots-Tag and the terms page, with the signal that decided each answer and every conflict between signals. Signed. Not legal advice.
descriptions.check_site_safety: Use when the only question is whether a site is listed as dangerous, before an agent reads, cites, links to or pays it. Returns whether it is listed as malware or phishing (Google Safe Browsing, a public malware-blocking DNS resolver, PhishTank), which list says so, where to check it and where its owner requests a review, plus HSTS preload and the hacked-site signatures from its latest CrawlCheck scan. An unread list is reported as unread, never as clean. For an allow/block decision on a specific action call preflight; for the full record call resolve_domain. Free, read-only.
descriptions.draft_llms: Draft an llms.txt from the domain's own homepage and up to 25 declared pages, using their titles and descriptions. A draft for the owner to cut down, not a publication.
descriptions.fix_robots: The domain's served robots.txt, corrected: * group rules copied into named groups that lacked them (shadowing), a Sitemap line added when missing, a minimal replacement when the served file was HTML. Every change is listed at the top; nothing else is touched.
descriptions.fix_entitymap: Use when a site has no entitymap.json, or to replace a wrong one. Returns a starter entitymap.json built from the domain's latest scan record: business name, phone, coordinates and declared service areas as entities with SERVES relations. Fields the site never stated are marked TODO, never guessed. Read-only; needs a prior scan of the domain (run scan_domain first if there is none).
descriptions.video_check: Use to audit one YouTube video for search and AI visibility. Returns twelve checks against the video anchor model (metadata, chapters, captions and storyboard where observed), each naming what it read and whether it passed. Read-only; results are cached for six hours unless fresh is true. For a channel's upload list use video_channel; for how a website embeds its videos use video_site.
descriptions.video_channel: Use to list a YouTube channel's uploads. Returns every upload on the channel, read 50 at a time and sorted by views. Give handle or, without one, the channel id. The per-check tally needs a Watch licence and is not offered here. Read-only. For the checks on one video use video_check.
descriptions.video_site: Use to check how a website carries its videos. Reads the homepage plus up to 60 sitemap pages for YouTube embeds, facades and page-builder widgets, VideoObject nodes and their required properties, and, given a channel handle, how many of the channel's videos the site carries. Read-only. For one video use video_check; for a channel's uploads use video_channel.
descriptions.registry_lookup: Whether a domain is in CrawlCheck's registry and what it serves: llms.txt, agents.md, a media kit at /.well-known/media-kit.json, a reciprocity-tested entity graph, an AI access policy that names crawlers, and agent-callable surfaces. With no domain, returns the shelf counts across every measured site. A row exists because a fetch produced it; nothing here is self-reported and no payment moves a shelf.
descriptions.crawler_path: Where each crawler's path into a domain dies, as an observed data flow: edge decision, robots.txt as a file, robots.txt rules, then the page, JSON-LD, sitemap, llms.txt and entitymap.json it reached. Give agent (e.g. ClaudeBot, GPTBot, googlebot) for one identity's path and a one-line answer; omit it for every identity plus the stores and breaks. Uses the latest record on file, or scans first when there is none (fresh=true forces a scan). The answer-engine output is drawn but never measured.
descriptions.public_counts: Use when you need to quote one of CrawlCheck's figures about itself. Returns them read from the source: sites_measured, domains_in_corpus, crawler_visits (a rolling window), sections, sections_scored, findings_published, guides_published, with an at timestamp. No input; read-only. For dataset coverage by stratum use corpus_state.
descriptions.telemetry: Verified-crawler traffic observed at crawlcheck.io itself: which named agents arrived, how many claims were confirmed against operator ranges, how many were forged.
descriptions.fix_mostly_code: A fix plan for PAGE_IS_MOSTLY_CODE: the homepage's measured bytes by category, the largest blocks with what to do with each, ordered steps with the text ratio after each, and the step at which the detector would stop firing - or, when moving code cannot clear it, how much markup to cut or text to add. Give domain (fetched now) or id (a stored scan).
descriptions.fix_stale_cache: Use after a scan reports STALE_CACHE_SERVED (visitors and crawlers get an old cached homepage). Fetches the homepage now and returns its Age, the cache layers that name themselves in the headers in purge order (innermost first), the HTML lifetime each response declares, a fresh-read comparison, and whether a purge clears the finding and keeps it cleared. Read-only; it does not purge anything. Give domain, or a report id (the page is still fetched now because cache state is live).
descriptions.fix_machine_chain: Use after a scan reports MACHINE_CHAIN_HEAVY (crawlers must read too many or too large files before the page). Returns a fix plan: the files a crawler reads before the page and the 404s that absent agent files return, then measured reductions (llms.txt to an index, a sitemap index, robots.txt comments and duplicate groups, minified JSON, short 404s) with the chain size after each step and the step at which the finding stops firing. Read-only; changes nothing on the site. Give domain (uses the latest scan on file) or a report id. For other findings use explain_finding.
descriptions.explain_finding: Why CrawlCheck decided a finding: the rule and its revision, the exact fetches it compared (identity, status, bytes, sha256), when the condition held on the site, and a Merkle proof that the decision is inside the signed manifest. Give id (a d1: decision or f1: finding id from a report), or domain alone for its top finding, or domain plus code for a named finding. Free, no key; read-only. A finding's age and history need a licence for that domain (send it in x-crawlcheck-key).
descriptions.machine_record: The unified machine record for one observation: subject, grade, findings (in full), capabilities with verification, and the evidence roots, manifest and verifier links that let anyone check it offline. Give id (report, d1:, f1: or manifest sha256) or domain for the latest.
descriptions.mcp_precheck: For MCP server publishers, before releasing a new version. Give the server name (as listed in the MCP Registry) or its endpoint, the new tools/list result and the new serverInfo.version; with no tools the endpoint is read as it serves now. Returns, against CrawlCheck's last read of that server, what public change logs will record: tools added and removed, descriptions rewritten, input schemas widened, annotations changed (read-only to write and non-destructive to destructive flagged as escalations), whether the version moved, and verdicts such as version_bump_needed or looks_like_rug_pull_risk. Signed. No tool on the checked server is called.

reading: Save this file beside the server's configuration. Before every connect, hash the current tools/list the same way and compare; anything different means the approved tools are not the tools that will run. POST it with the current list to /api/v1/mcp/lock/check for a signed record of the comparison.

signature.canonical: sha256 over canonical JSON of every field except sha256 and signature
